# OpenRouter

A single OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint in front of many vendors' models, billed per token against
one account. In [[agent-orchestrator]] it is the **router**: the model that plans, answers directly
when a request does not need agents, writes the optional workspace brief, and merges the finished
subtasks.

## The property the design leans on

The router is the one component that reads every subtask's output — and it has **no tools at all**.
That asymmetry is the security model's load-bearing claim: text that persuades the router can produce
a wrong answer but cannot produce an action. The executors have the tools; the reader has none.

## No vendor is named in code

The model id is configuration (`z-ai/glm-5.2` by default, any id OpenRouter serves). At start-up the
backend resolves the display name, context window and reasoning support from `/models`, and if the id
is absent from that catalog it still uses it and logs a line saying so. So switching router is a
settings change, and a model released next week works without a code change.

Where a configured router advertises no reasoning parameter, none is sent — the same restraint as
[[reasoning-effort-as-a-portable-label]] one level up.

## Cost and key handling

Only these calls cost money: roughly $0.002 for a two-subtask run, because the agents themselves run
on the user's existing CLI subscriptions ([[claude-code-cli]], [[codex-cli]]). The key lives in VS
Code's encrypted SecretStorage, reaches the backend as an environment variable, and is never sent to
the webview — [[secrets-from-environment-only]]. The plaintext settings field still works and the
panel offers to migrate it, because a key already typed into settings is a fact to handle, not a
mistake to lecture about.
